22: ### What's new in v0.2.3
23: 
24: - **iOS touch settings:** touch navigation stays available while settings are open and returns cleanly to gameplay afterward.
25: - **Hybrid cutscenes:** the character screen stays enlarged through dialogue and dialogue gaps. Chapter cards also promote the bottom screen when the top screen is blank, and brief scene-state changes no longer flash the background into focus.
26: - **FPS meter:** the on-screen frame-rate badge remains available at the top right, including on iPhone and iPad.
27: 
28: - **Widescreen and hybrid display:** native 16:10, 16:9, and 21:9 dungeon
29:   rendering, expanded camera/tile streaming, anchored HUD elements, and a
30:   single-window layout with a small second-screen inset.
31: - **Smoother motion:** camera and entity interpolation for 120Hz, 144Hz, and
32:   240Hz displays, with uncapped VRR available.
33: - **Visual options:** pixel-art filters, LCD and CRT effects, and weather-aware
34:   dungeon lighting.
35: - **Configurable inputs:** separate Video, Controller, Keyboard, and System
36:   settings pages; assign individual controller or keyboard inputs, choose
37:   presets, restore defaults, and save settings between launches.
38: - **iPhone and iPad support:** native ROM import and on-device compilation,
39:   touch controls, Files-accessible saves/logs, and a gear button for settings.
40: 
41: > **Clean-Room & Legal Notice:** This repository contains **zero** copyrighted Nintendo DS ROMs, extracted assets, BIOS/firmware dumps, or ROM-derived C code. Players must supply their own legally dumped *Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Sky* `.nds` cartridge image. No Nintendo DS BIOS or firmware files are required (`FreeBIOS` + synthesized NVRAM direct boot).
42: 
43: ---
44: 
45: ## Features & Roadmap
46: 
47: - **Milestone 1 (Pre-Alpha -- Active):** Native **macOS Apple Silicon (`arm64`)** static recompilation of all **34 executable modules** (`arm9`, `itcm`, `arm7` + WRAM/RAM drivers, and all 32 active overlays -- `91,872` recompiled functions), BIOS-free direct boot, 128 KiB FRAM/EEPROM saves, savestates, audio, and controller support.
48: - **Milestone 2:** Native **Windows (`x86_64`)** and **Linux (`x86_64` / `arm64`)** builds & packaging.
49: - **Milestone 3:** **Beyond-Emulator Graphics & Smoothness** -- True `16:9` / `21:9` native 2D widescreen (`overlay29` & `overlay11` camera/tile hooks + anchored HUD), **120Hz / 144Hz / 240Hz** sub-pixel camera & sprite interpolation, and custom Apple Metal / `SDL_GPU` pixel-art & weather shaders.
50: - **Milestone 4:** **Launcher, SkyTemple Mod Loader & Online Rescue Board** -- Zero-recompile layered NitroFS mod overrides, SkyTemple custom ASM hack recompilation, and an asynchronous *Rescue Team DX*-style Online Rescue Bulletin Board backed by vanilla **Wonder Mail S / SOS / A-OK Mail** structs (with 54-character passwords preserved forever as an offline fallback).
51: - **Milestone 5 (Planned):** **Cross-Device Saves & Graphics Backends** -- iCloud save synchronization between iOS and macOS devices, plus Vulkan support for the custom pixel-art and weather shader pipeline alongside Metal.
52: 
53: See [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full technical specification.
54: 
55: ### Opening and using in-game settings
56: 
57: Press **F1** during gameplay, or press **Guide** on a controller. You can also
58: open settings with **Select+Start**. On iPhone or iPad, tap the **⚙** button in
59: the on-screen controls. The settings open on the category list:
60: **Video**, **Controller**, **Keyboard**, and **System**. Use the arrow keys or
61: D-pad to choose a category and press **Enter** or **A** to open it. Press
62: **Escape** or **B/Back** to return to the category list; press it again to close
63: settings.
64: 
65: In **Controller** or **Keyboard**, select an action such as **A** or **Up** and
66: press **Enter** or **A**. Then press the controller button, move the stick, or
67: press the keyboard key you want to assign. **Backspace** clears a binding;
68: **Escape** or **Guide** cancels assignment. Each page has a **Restore defaults**
69: action. On iOS, a connected keyboard or controller can assign inputs; the touch
70: controls remain available on screen.
71: 
72: ### Can I play a European ROM in another language?
73: 
74: The European cartridge includes English, French, German, Italian, and Spanish.
75: SkyRecompiled's generated firmware currently selects English, so the European
76: game starts in English. A **Game language** setting is planned for Explorers
77: of Sky’s own options menu. It will show the languages available on your
78: cartridge and apply your choice on the next launch. The USA release contains
79: English game text.
80: 
81: ---
82: 
83: ## Quickstart (macOS Apple Silicon)
84: 
85: ### Prerequisites
86: ```bash
87: brew install cmake ninja sdl3 python
88: ```
89: 
90: ### Build and launch
91: 
92: Supply a clean USA or Europe ROM. Bootstrap the pinned tools, compile the game,
93: and package the macOS app:
94: 
95: ```bash
96: ./scripts/setup_third_party.sh
97: python3 scripts/build.py --rom "/path/to/Explorers of Sky.nds" --package
98: open build/SkyRecompiled.app
99: ```
100: 
101: For the offline translator and runtime build layout, see [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md#build-layout).
102: 
103: ---
104: 
105: ## Quickstart (Windows x64)
106: 
107: You can download the pre-packaged Windows release above (which runs cartridge code at runtime) or build the runner locally with your own clean *Explorers of Sky* USA or Europe ROM to include statically recompiled game code.
108: 
109: Install Python 3.12+, Git for Windows (with Git Bash available on PATH), and [MSYS2](https://www.msys2.org/). In the **MSYS2 MINGW64** shell, install the build tools:
110: 
111: ```bash
112: pacman -S --needed mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc mingw-w64-x86_64-cmake mingw-w64-x86_64-ninja
113: ```
114: 
115: Extract **`SDL3-devel-3.4.14-mingw.zip`** from the [SDL3 release page](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/releases/tag/release-3.4.14). In PowerShell, run these commands from the repository root. Adjust the paths to match your installation and ROM.
116: 
117: ```powershell
118: & "${env:ProgramFiles}\Git\bin\bash.exe" scripts/setup_third_party.sh
119: $env:Path = "C:\msys64\mingw64\bin;$env:Path"
120: python scripts/build.py --sdl3-sdk "C:\path\to\SDL3-3.4.14" --rom "C:\path\to\Explorers of Sky.nds"
121: python scripts/launcher.py --rom "C:\path\to\Explorers of Sky.nds"
122: ```
123: 
124: After the build succeeds, `& .\build\runner\nds_runner.exe --help` checks that the runner starts. To create a local ZIP, run `python scripts/package_release.py --platform windows`. Extract the whole ZIP before opening `SkyRecompiled.bat`.
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## iPhone and iPad
129: 
130: Download the pre-built `SkyRecompiled-v0.2.3-ios.ipa` from the [v0.2.3 GitHub Release](https://github.com/DarthMDev/pmd-sky-recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.3), or build from source on a Mac with Xcode, CMake, Ninja, and Python 3:
131: 
132: ```bash
133: python3 scripts/build_ios.py
134: ```
135: 
136: The build writes `build/ios/SkyRecompiled-iOS-alpha.ipa` (or package for distribution with `python3 scripts/package_release.py --platform ios`). The **iOS alpha IPA**
137: GitHub Actions workflow builds and verifies this same artifact on push to `main` and pull requests.
138: 
139: 1. SkyRecompiled requires iOS or iPadOS 16.0 or later. Set up AltStore Classic
140:    on your iPhone or iPad and enable Developer Mode. [AltStore setup for macOS](https://faq.altstore.io/altstore-classic/how-to-install-altstore-macos)
141: 2. Save the IPA to Files. In AltStore, open **My Apps**, tap **+**, and select
142:    the IPA. AltStore signs it for your device. Refresh it before the signing
143:    expires. [AltStore signing and refresh](https://faq.altstore.io/altstore-classic/your-altstore)
144: 3. Open SkyRecompiled, choose **Import ROM from Files**, and select your own
145:    clean USA or Europe Explorers of Sky `.nds` dump. Tap **Compile and Play**.
146:    Use the on-screen controls or connect a controller. Tap **Launcher** to exit
147:    the game and flush pending saves.
148: 4. In **Files → On My iPhone/iPad → SkyRecompiled**, find `Logs/latest.log`
149:    after launching the app and `Saves/pmdsky.sav` after the game creates a save.
150:    The iOS software renderer uses the native 1× resolution.
151: 
152: The iOS app reuses the desktop runner and compiles ROM instructions into portable
153: intermediate code on the device. It can run without JIT signing privileges.
154: This alpha uses the runner's interpreter for that code, so performance may
155: differ from the native desktop build.
156: 
157: For Apple silicon Mac testing, boot an iPhone or iPad in Simulator, then run
158: these commands from the repository root. Simulator sets up the runtime the
159: app needs at launch.
160: 
161: ```bash
162: python3 scripts/build_ios.py --simulator
163: xcrun simctl install booted build/ios/simulator/SkyRecompiled.app
164: xcrun simctl launch booted dev.skyrecompiled.ios
165: ```
166: 
167: Running the iOS build directly on an Apple silicon Mac requires Apple development
168: or distribution signing. [Apple silicon iOS app testing](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple-silicon/running-your-ios-apps-in-macos)
169: 
170: ---
171: 
172: ## AI Usage & Verification Disclaimer
173: 
174: AI coding tools were used during the development of this project. All translated and recompiled output is rigorously verified against real Nintendo DS hardware and reference emulator behavior:
175: - **100% Executable Coverage:** All 34 executable modules (`arm9`, `itcm`, `arm7` + WRAM/RAM drivers, and all 32 active overlays -- 91,872 functions) compile natively with zero unimplemented instructions.
176: - **Hardware-Synced Logic:** Over 99.9% of guest instructions execute through native static C code with zero RAM code rejects. Game logic, turn execution, deterministic RNG, and cartridge FRAM/EEPROM saves are verified against hardware behavior and melonDS references via automated test suites.

1: # Milestone 4 implementation plan
2: 
3: Local planning document — 2026-11-11. Source inspection only; no builds, tests, network checks, or deployment verification performed. “Implemented” below means code exists, not that its runtime behavior has passed acceptance. No Milestone 4 feature is established as end-to-end complete by this audit.
4: 
5: ## Current-state audit and status reconciliation
6: 
7: - **Desktop launcher — partial, with substantive implementation.** `src/SkyRecompiled.Launcher/Views/MainWindow.axaml`, `ViewModels/MainViewModel.cs`, and `Services/RomPreparationService.cs` provide an Avalonia ROM picker, clean NA/EU SHA-1 verification, remembered path, runner discovery, process launch, save paths, and log capture. Launch progress includes artificial delays; it does not perform compilation despite UI wording. The process is not monitored to completion; resetting the ROM does not clear persisted selection; settings writes replace the whole file. There is no mod manager or rescue board in this UI. `scripts/launcher.py` supplies another launch path with package/repository discovery and clean-ROM validation. Packaging parity and the canonical launcher remain unresolved.
8: - **Layered NitroFS — implemented tooling, missing demonstrated runtime integration.** `tools/sky_mod_packer.py` parses FNT/FAT, extracts files, applies layers sorted by `(priority, id)` (higher priority wins; later ID wins ties), and emits FNT/FAT/payload. It does not itself make the runner consume these outputs. Neither inspected launcher passes mod inputs; the searched first-party `runtime/` sources expose no NitroFS override integration. The actual upstream cartridge-read integration point still needs inspection during implementation. Repacking assigns new file IDs and needs compatibility work before serving game reads. Metadata uses a hand-written TOML subset; layer input symlinks and malformed ROM tables need stronger validation. `tests/test_nitrofs.py` has parse/priority/rebuild checks, but its class-wide ROM prerequisite also skips synthetic tests when the ROM is absent.
9: - **SkyTemple ASM — partial translator support, not general hack compatibility.** `translator/prepare_rom.py` accepts custom ROMs only with `--allow-custom-rom --region NA|EU`, decompresses ARM9/overlays, and produces bank configurations/C through its compilation path. Overlay iteration uses the actual table length, not a hard-coded 0–35 limit: overlay 36 can enter the same pipeline, even without a symbol YAML file. Heuristic entry discovery and clean-ROM symbol assumptions do not prove arbitrary modified code works. `scripts/build.py` still invokes preparation through its clean-ROM flow; both inspected launchers reject modified hashes. Custom identity, cache isolation, hook compatibility, packaging, and runtime verification remain incomplete.
10: - **Rescue — backend scaffold and provisional codec, missing client/game integration.** `tools/wondermail.py` implements 34-character mission and 54-character rescue encoders/decoders, including a Thank-You kind. Rescue encoding uses its own field packing, padding, and Fletcher-style checksum; `tests/test_wondermail.py` mainly establishes internal round trips, not vanilla interoperability. `services/rescue-worker/src/index.ts` implements posting/listing/getting, timed claims, and A-OK completion against `schema.sql`. Completion compares dungeon/floor, not the decoded rescue identity; no ownership authorization is enforced. The 32-bit rescue-ID bit reader needs explicit width tests. Python normalization filters characters differently from the worker. There is no Thank-You storage/route in the schema/handler, no launcher board or inspected runtime mail bridge, and no worker test script in `package.json`. Public listing exposes whole rows, including optional friend codes. Rate limits, retention, moderation, and budget controls are not established by this scaffold.
11: 
12: **Reconciliation:** `TASKS_FLASH_MEDIUM.md` marks Batches 4–5 complete, but explicitly describes “Mod Loader Tooling” and a backend “scaffold.” Credit those artifacts as implemented foundations, not completion of playable mod loading or online rescue. Its overlay-36 detection claim is supported narrowly by table-driven translator handling, not a verified full ASM workflow. `README.md` still presents Milestone 4 as roadmap work; that remains the defensible product status. `ARCHITECTURE.md` describes intended runtime interception/direct RAM mail integration and makes broader compatibility and hosting claims than the inspected code proves. Its claimed live URL is not verified here. It also calls 54-character codes Wonder Mail S, whereas the tool separates 34-character mission codes and 54-character rescue codes. Resolve terminology against vanilla evidence before publishing documentation. Update public status only after the gates below; leave the local task queue untouched by this planning task.
13: 
14: ## Scope and decisions to settle
15: 
16: **Proposed scope:** one supported desktop launcher; deterministic, startup-applied NitroFS replacement layers without recompiling executable banks; explicit local recompilation for a tested subset of SkyTemple ARM9/overlay hacks, including overlay 36 where present; an opt-in asynchronous rescue board transporting verified vanilla SOS/A-OK/Thank-You data. Keep classic password entry/display usable without a service.
17: 
18: **Assumptions:** target existing desktop platforms, with NA first and EU gated by evidence; first mod slice replaces existing assets only; first rescue slice uses manual password transfer through existing game menus. These are proposals, not existing capabilities. The complete milestone includes all four areas, even if delivered incrementally.
19: 
20: **Exclusions:** iOS launcher redesign, real-time co-op/WFC emulation, mandatory accounts, mod marketplace/automatic downloads, arbitrary native plugins, live ASM hot swapping, universal hack compatibility, and distribution of ROMs/extracted assets/generated game code. iCloud save synchronization between iOS and macOS is tracked separately as a planned milestone, not part of Milestone 4. Vulkan shader support is also tracked separately. Adding/deleting NitroFS paths and automatic guest-memory injection follow the basic slices only if explicitly selected; neither is needed to prove replacement loading or password-based rescue.
21: 
22: Settle these architectural contracts before dependent work:
23: 
24: - Choose Avalonia versus existing platform launch wrappers, and a shared profile/settings/save-location contract. Prefer extending Avalonia and preserving current save discovery/migration, subject to owner approval.
25: - Inspect the pinned runner's cartridge and NitroFS read path. Select interception or a virtual cartridge view that preserves guest-visible IDs, offsets, and executable overlay reads. Separate asset substitution from executable module identity; do not assume a new runner flag already exists.
26: - Specify versioned mod metadata, enabled layers, unique IDs, precedence, conflicts, supported base hashes, and file-path rules. Preserve current higher-priority-wins semantics with an explicit deterministic tie rule and a visible conflict report.

1: # European ROM language support
2: 
3: On a DS, the European release of *Explorers of Sky* follows the system's
4: language setting. SkyRecompiled generates a firmware image with that setting
5: fixed to English. The translations are in the European cartridge. Direct boot
6: copies the effective firmware user settings into guest RAM at `0x027FFC80`,
7: where the game can read them. This path uses FreeBIOS and generated firmware.
8: [Nintendo DS language settings](https://en-americas-support.nintendo.com/app/answers/detail/p/606/c/898/a_id/7398)
9: 
10: ## In-game settings design
11: 
12: Expose **Game language** in Explorers of Sky’s own options menu for every
13: supported cartridge. Offer the choices available for the active ROM in their
14: own language. The verified USA ROM (`C2SE`) contains only English game text.
15: The verified European ROM (`C2SP`) supports all five choices below. Persist
16: the preference in the host runtime settings and default to English. If the
17: active ROM lacks the preferred language, use English for that session and
18: retain the saved preference.
19: 
20: | Choice | DS firmware ID |
21: | --- | ---: |
22: | English | 1 |
23: | Français | 2 |
24: | Deutsch | 3 |
25: | Italiano | 4 |
26: | Español | 5 |
27: 
28: Show **Applies on next launch** after changing the setting. The game chooses
29: localized resources during startup. Applying the preference at the next boot
30: keeps resource initialization on the normal guest path and lets players save
31: their progress before closing the game. Existing savestates resume guest RAM
32: from the language active when they were captured.
33: 
34: ## Runner integration
35: 
36: 1. Parse and validate the saved preference before boot. Use English when there
37:    is no preference or the validated ROM identity lacks the preferred language.
38: 2. For generated firmware, apply the preference after any firmware state is
39:    loaded and before `nds_direct_boot` mirrors the settings. Update bits 0–2
40:    of the little-endian language and flags word at offset `0x64` in each user
41:    settings copy. Preserve the other flags and update each copy's checksum
42:    using the same routine as the existing player-name setter.
43:    [DS firmware user settings format](https://doc.kodewerx.org/documents/gbatek.html)
44: 3. Unit test both settings copies, checksum recalculation, preservation of
45:    unrelated bytes, and the default and invalid preference paths using
46:    generated firmware. With a locally supplied European ROM, confirm the
47:    selection persists across a relaunch and the title and dialogue use the
48:    selected language. Confirm a cartridge save still loads after switching.
